title: Go: Channels Basics
description: Learn to create, send on, and receive from Go channels for goroutine communication.

steps.title: Create a channel
steps.description: Use `make(chan int)` to create an unbuffered channel of integers. Print the channel's type and value using `fmt.Printf("%T, %v\n", ch, ch)`.
hints: An unbuffered channel blocks on send until someone receives
Printing a channel shows its pointer address

verification.successMessage: Channel created and its type is displayed!
verification.failureMessage: Make sure to print the type with %T.

steps.title: Send and receive
steps.description: In a goroutine send the value 42 on a channel. In main receive it and print "Received: 42".
hints: Unbuffered channels synchronize — the goroutine won't send until main is ready to receive

verification.successMessage: Send and receive worked as a synchronous hand-off!
verification.failureMessage: Make sure you send from a goroutine and receive in main.

steps.title: Blocking nature
steps.description: Demonstrate blocking by having main try to send on an unbuffered channel without a receiver. Print "Before send" before the send and note the deadlock. Then fix by using a goroutine receiver.
hints: An unbuffered channel send blocks until another goroutine receives
Without a receiver, the program deadlocks — Go detects this at runtime
Wrap the receive in a goroutine: `go func() { ... }()`

verification.successMessage: You demonstrated unbuffered channel blocking behavior!
verification.failureMessage: Print 'Before send' before the send operation.

steps.title: Channel direction
steps.description: Write a function `producer(ch chan<- int)` that sends values 1, 2, 3 on the channel. In main, receive and print them using `consumer(ch <-chan int)`.
hints: Use `chan<-` for send-only and `<-chan` for receive-only parameters
Directional channels prevent misuse at compile time
Close the channel in the producer when done

verification.successMessage: Channel directions enforce safe goroutine communication!
verification.failureMessage: Make sure you implement both producer and consumer functions.

steps.title: Close a channel
steps.description: Open a channel, send two values ("hello" and "world") from a goroutine, then close it. In main, use `val, ok := <-ch` to detect when the channel is closed and print "channel closed".
hints: Close with `close(ch)` from the sender side
The receive returns `ok = false` when the channel is closed and empty
Only the sender should close a channel, never the receiver

verification.successMessage: You correctly detected a closed channel using the ok idiom!
verification.failureMessage: Remember to use `val, ok := <-ch` to check if the channel is closed.
